# TouchDesigner Python Rules

The rules that prevent the common mistakes. The API detail, code patterns and measurements live in `/td-api-reference`; load it before writing TD Python.

## Verify before claiming

Never assume a TD feature, API, file type or convention exists: `describe_op_type` for parameter names, `get_docs` for the official page, a live probe through `execute_python` for behavior. A claim about TD you have not verified is a guess; say so.

## Parameters

`parameters.md` holds the value rules (`.eval()`, `.val` switches the mode, toggles are `0`/`1`, explicit casts) and the OP-reference conventions.

## Naming

- Name things for what they do: `EnsureCatalogs()`, `RestoreSettings()`, never `CheckAndX()`, `Process()`, `Handle()`. No implementation leakage (`ParseJSONAndUpdateTable` is `RefreshOpList`), no abbreviated domain terms (`ComputeTDXNFingerprint`, not `CalcTDXNFp`), booleans read as questions (`hasExternalWires()`). Write the one-line docstring first: if the name is not in it, the name is wrong.
- Operators: `optype_name` for processing ops (`glsl_colorize`, `noise_terrain`, `null_out`). Exempt: COMPs reached by a shortcut or holding an extension (`Embody`), contract-fixed terminals (`out1`), and DATs, which stay role-named (`tdxn_exporter`; a DAT named `json` also shadows the stdlib).

## Extension namespaces: three tiers

TD promotes EVERY capitalized member of a promoted extension onto the COMP, methods and class constants alike, so the capital letter is the access modifier:

| Tier | Name | Reached as | Who calls it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Public API | `UpperCamelCase` | `op.Comp.Method()` | a user or an agent, deliberately |
| 2 Wiring | `lowerCamelCase` | `op.Comp.ext.Name.method()` | the COMP's own exec, callback and parexec DATs |
| 3 Private | `_lowerCamelCase` | inside the class | the class itself |

The test: could a user or an agent reasonably call this ON the COMP? If not, it is not tier 1; frame hooks, contact routers, dispatchers and `ensurePars` are tier 2. Co-mounted extensions share one namespace (a duplicate promoted name silently wins), every promoted name is a `getattr` dispatch target (dispatchers must check `callable()`), and a promoted name is published API. `.ext.<Name>` resolves by the Extension Name parameter, not the class name (`op.Embody.ext.Embody`, never `.ext.EmbodyExt`). Capitalized class constants are promoted too: put them at module level or name them `_UPPER`. A name reached only from a `run()` string, a parameter expression or DAT text inside a `.toe` stays tier 1 until every call site is rewritten; demote behind a fail-loud call site, never a `hasattr` guard. (Model from Function Store, issue #94; detail in `/create-extension`.)

## Type hints

Annotate every `def`, arguments and return, with TD's classes as the types (`COMP`, `DAT`, `Par`, `constantCHOP`); `Optional[str] = None`, never `str = None`; `-> None` for callbacks. `opex(...).asType(levelTOP, checkType=True)` is the typed, runtime-asserted read. Detail: `/td-api-reference` (Type Hints).

## Operator access and referencing

- `opex()` when the operator must exist (it raises clearly); `op()` returns `None` silently.
- Never call `op()`, `parent()` or touch TD objects at module level; module code runs at import, before the network is ready.
- Absolute paths (`op('/project1/...')`) are always wrong, in code, expressions AND parameter values. Take the highest rung that resolves: `self.ownerComp` inside an extension; `parent.CompName` from the COMP's own DATs and expressions (set `par.parentshortcut` on every reusable COMP); `op('sibling')` and `op('./child')`; `iop.Name` / `ipar.Name` for published internal addresses; `op.CompName` for project-wide singletons only. The bare global `parent()` / `parent(N)` is banned in an extension class body (exemptions: a COMP's own callback DAT, generic tooling in a COMP it did not author, expressions on replicated widgets).
- After ANY rename (operator, method or parameter) sweep every live surface, not just DAT text on disk: DAT text inside the `.toe` (`findChildren(type=DAT)`), `par.expr`, `par.bindExpr`, constant-mode OP-reference values (`par.val`), and `run()` strings. `findChildren(depth=N)` matches EXACTLY depth N; walk with no depth argument or `maxDepth=N`.

## Extensions

- Implement `onDestroyTD(self)` (teardown) and `onInitTD(self)` (post-init); extensions reinitialize on every source save.
- Route parameter callbacks through ONE dispatcher (`_on<Par>ValueChange(par, prev)` / `_on<Par>Pulse(par)` found by `getattr`, a miss logged), never an `elif par.name` chain of promoted methods (`/parameter-design`).
- Inside a TDXN-strategy COMP `onInitTD` fires BEFORE the import rebuilds the children: defer with `run(..., delayFrames=5)`, stay idempotent, null-check children, keep durable state outside the boundary.
- A parameter expression that reads a promoted attribute guards with `parent().X if parent().extensionsReady else 0`.

## Threading

A worker thread touches NO TD object, and a read counts as a write: no `op()`, no `Par` (not even `.eval()`), no DAT/CHOP/SOP/TOP content, no `storage`, no `tdu.Dependency`, no `debug()`/`print()`, and never `run()` from a worker (it does not raise; the crash lands later, far from the call site; Derivative-confirmed 2026-08-17). Fetch with a native operator (Web Client DAT), chunk long main-thread work with `run(delayFrames=N)`, and use the Thread Manager only for pure-Python work with a main-thread drain. The ladder and the code: `/td-api-reference` (Background and Long-Running Work) and its `references/background-work.md`.

## Cook model

Pull-based: operators cook when something demands their output, so a time-dependent op with no viewer, Render TOP or Out TOP demanding it sits frozen on its last frame (the number-one cause of "it is not animating"). `cook(force=True)` does not advance a feedback loop within a frame; a Movie File In reload lands only across a real frame advance; a CHOP Execute DAT is a per-frame demand source. Detail: `/td-api-reference` (Cook Model Gotchas).

## State

User-facing state is a custom parameter; hidden durable bookkeeping is `storage` (on the COMP, survives a reinit, wiped when the contents are replaced by a tox reload or TDXN rebuild); a derived value that must recook its readers is a `tdu.Dependency` (dies with the extension instance; rebuild it in `__init__`). Write through `store()` (`comp.storage[k] = v` notifies nobody), `dep.val = 5` (`dep = 5` destroys it), `.modified()` after an in-place mutation; `fetch()` without a default RAISES and searches UP the parents; `unstore()` is glob-matched. Publish once and let readers pull; never push values into consumers. Measurements: `/parameter-design` and its `references/state-lifetimes.md`.

## Everyday

- `debug()` over `print()`; `mod.name` re-resolves every call (cache it in loops); `changeType()` returns the new op; `copyOPs([list])` keeps wires, `COMP.copy()` does not; `addError()`/`addWarning()` work only in cook callbacks; `TOP.sample()` downloads the whole texture (use `numpyArray()`).
- Render coordinates: (0, 0) is bottom-left with Y up for `TOP.sample`, GLSL, UVs, Crop/Transform parameters AND `numpyArray()` rows (row 0 is the bottom; measured 2025.33230). PIL/OpenCV images and panel coordinates are top-down; `np.flipud` converts.
- `requests` blocks the frame: never on the main thread (see Threading).
